item.title: Africa: Trading in yuan
item.description: The dollar has long ruled Africa's financial landscape. But as more countries turn to China's yuan, the balance of economic power could be shifting.

item.title: Bagel makers, lovers and critics converged in New York for best bagel contest
item.description: The best bagel contest in New York City last weekend drew competitors from around the world, and of course lots of hometown bagel makers and critics.

item.title: Brain cell mapping lays groundwork for better treatments for conditions like dementia
item.description: A major effort from brain researchers around the world has yielded a cellular atlas of the basal ganglia — structures key to learning and controlling motor skills.

item.title: Questions about FAA funding roil Capitol Hill after nationwide ground stop
item.description: Three days after a communications meltdown led the FAA to ground planes, there are big questions about what happened and how much money is needed to upgrade the country's air traffic control system.

item.title: A meteorite hit her home. She's showing it to Houston: 'I want everybody to see it'
item.description: Earlier this year, a meteorite crashed into the home of a Houston-area woman. Most of the meteor burned up, but 19 fragments were found and are on display at the Houston Museum of Natural Science.

item.title: New rule aims to close loophole on chip exports
item.description: The Commerce Department released a new rule designed to make it harder for China to gain access to America's most powerful computer chips using third-country data centers.

item.title: Pope Leo XIV wraps up demanding, emotional Latin America tour
item.description: After visiting three countries and 10 cities, Pope Leon XIV is headed back to Rome. He wrapped up the 12-day tour with an emotional send off in Peru, his second homeland.

item.title: If Robert Pattinson is James Bond, 007 needs to get a little weird
item.description: Amazon announced Monday that Robert Pattinson will be the next James Bond. NPR critic Glen Weldon says the idiosyncratic actor would seem to be a better fit as a Bond villain.
